cards.design_implication: If the research objective is to isolate the impact of specific feedback or star formation models on galaxy properties, a study design could implement a code-comparison framework where initial conditions are fixed while varying only the sub-grid physics implementations across different hydrodynamical schemes.
does_not_establish: The specific statistical methods used for analysis.
The detailed calibration procedures for the individual codes.
The causal mechanisms within the codes beyond the comparative outcome.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We compare the results of various cosmological gas-dynamical codes used to simulate the formation of a galaxy in the Λ cold dark matter structure formation paradigm. The various runs (13 in total) differ in their numerical hydrodynamical treatment [smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), moving mesh and adaptive mesh refinement] but share the same initial conditions and adopt in each case their latest published model of gas cooling, star formation and feedback.
limitations: The study design is specific to cosmological simulations of a single galaxy formation scenario.
It relies on pre-existing codes with different numerical hydrodynamical treatments.
The comparison involves 13 runs, which may not cover all possible model variations.
cards.statement: The study compares results from 13 cosmological gas-dynamical codes simulating galaxy formation in the Lambda cold dark matter paradigm, which share the same initial conditions but differ in numerical hydrodynamical treatments (SPH, moving mesh, AMR) and adopt their latest published models for gas cooling, star formation, and feedback.

cards.design_implication: A research design aiming to predict galaxy morphology could prioritize the selection and tuning of feedback mechanisms over other numerical parameters, given that feedback prescriptions induce larger variations in outcomes than differences in numerical techniques like grid-based vs. SPH.
does_not_establish: The exact causal chain within a single simulation run.
The universal applicability of this mechanism outside the LCDM paradigm.
The precise definition of 'star formation efficiency' or 'feedback strength' parameters.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Despite the common halo assembly history, we find large code-to-code variations in the stellar mass, size, morphology and gas content of the galaxy at z= 0, due mainly to the different implementations of star formation and feedback.
limitations: This is an observation from simulation comparisons, not an experimental manipulation of physical mechanisms in a lab.
The extent to which these mechanisms apply to real astrophysical systems is inferred from agreement with observations.
The specific mathematical details of the 'different implementations' are not provided.
cards.statement: Differences in the implementations of star formation and feedback are identified as the main drivers of code-to-code variations in galaxy properties (stellar mass, size, morphology, gas content) at z=0.

cards.design_implication: If relying on simulations for predictive models of galaxy formation, the research design must include uncertainty quantification across multiple codes or feedback models, rather than treating a single simulation output as a unique prediction.
does_not_establish: That simulations are entirely useless or non-reproducible.
The exact level of prediction error quantified in statistical terms.
Whether future methods will resolve this ambiguity.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We conclude that state-of-the-art simulations cannot yet uniquely predict the properties of the baryonic component of a galaxy, even when the assembly history of its host halo is fully specified.
limitations: This conclusion applies to the specific set of codes and models compared in the study.
It refers to the baryonic component specifically, not necessarily the dark matter component.
The limitation is based on current state-of-the-art methods described in the text.
cards.statement: State-of-the-art simulations cannot yet uniquely predict the properties of the baryonic component of a galaxy, even when the assembly history of its host halo is fully specified, due to code-to-code variations.

cards.design_implication: A study design could limit the resolution sweep to two specific numerical resolutions for code-comparison analyses if the primary goal is to verify that relative code differences persist across resolution scales, rather than achieving high-convergence standards.
does_not_establish: The specific resolution parameters (e.g., cell size, particle number).
The degree of uncertainty introduced by non-convergence.
Whether the conclusions hold at other, untested resolutions.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Although numerical convergence is not particularly good for any of the codes, our conclusions hold at two different numerical resolutions.
limitations: The text does not specify what the 'two different numerical resolutions' were.
The lack of good convergence within individual codes means absolute values may still be uncertain.
This applies only to the comparisons made in this specific study.
cards.statement: The study's conclusions hold at two different numerical resolutions, despite numerical convergence not being particularly good for any of the individual codes.
